rationale: This is a single-operator variant (RANK→IND_RANK on the conditioner) of the already-evaluated EarningPowerUnderChronicLiquidityVolatility, and since IND_RANK preserves the same monotone non-negative weighting within industries it is far more likely to yield a cosmetic re-estimate than a distinct economic test.

The expression is internally consistent and the conjunction of an income-statement and a balance-sheet conditioner has not been tested, but both conditioners are individually archived and the multiplicative rank weight makes it a fairly predictable hybrid of two known results (also note RANK(NEG(pi/at)) is a low-profitability ranking, not the "current pretax loss" the hypothesis asserts).

A coherent and cleanly specified generalisation of the instability conditioner to an income-statement second moment, though it edges toward the well-documented result that profitability/quality premia are concentrated among high-earnings-volatility, high-limits-to-arbitrage firms, so a positive outcome would be only weakly novel.

Internally consistent and the asset-scaled quality composite paired with the volatility conditioner is untested, but it is essentially a stack of two already-validated components (and the reasoning misstates the revenue-scaled composite as "failed" when it produced the archive's strongest FMB slope), so the marginal information is modest.

The most substantively new proposal in the batch: it relocates the uncertainty source from the balance-sheet residual to the sales process, which is a genuine discriminating test of whether working-capital volatility has merely been proxying for demand volatility, and the expression matches the hypothesis with the correct sign.

Multiplying the level and the five-year volatility of the same wcap/at variable — both already archived as conditioners and mechanically correlated through scale — is very likely to produce a signal statistically indistinguishable from the volatility-only version, making this an incremental recombination rather than a new mechanism.
